name: potassium inwardly rectifying channel subfamily J member 12

function.text: KCNJ12 is the approved symbol for potassium inwardly rectifying channel subfamily J member 12. Reviewed functional annotations implicate its product in inward rectifier potassium channel activity; muscle contraction; potassium ion import across plasma membrane.

germline.text: No conflict-free strong or definitive constitutional disease relationship met the source-selection criteria for this draft; this does not exclude a germline association.

somatic.text: Cancer Hotspots v1 reports recurrent residue-level observations in Adrenocortical carcinoma; Breast carcinoma; Colorectal carcinoma. This is statistical recurrence evidence; it does not establish that every variant in this gene is a driver or a clinically actionable alteration. Evidence in this collection is restricted to the historical V1 release.

function.text: KCNJ12 encodes potassium inwardly rectifying channel subfamily J member 12. Its functions include inward rectifier potassium channel activity and muscle contraction.

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving KCNJ12 have been reported in breast carcinoma, colorectal carcinoma, and adrenocortical carcinoma.
